claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x: the Pollard rho algorithm over order-6 automorphism equivalence classes (negation and GLV endomorphism) with distinguished points in proof.md, revised in v3 with a partition-bump step function that destroys the systematic two-cycle family of the v2 walk, an enforced bounded-retry treatment of exceptional steps, and split-coordinate scalar bookkeeping under a specified rebalancing schedule, succeeds with probability at least 0.405 using at most 2^127.22 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, all trials and failures, distinguished-point handling and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^113 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^27 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. The success bound relies on the disclosed random-mapping heuristic H1 stated in claim.json and proof.md, narrowed in v3 to collision statistics and per-step uniformity, with the walk's cycle structure proved separately in proof.md Section 6 and supported by the included toy experiment at its stated scope; every other step of the argument is exact. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic attack estimate under the fixed cost model, not an executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Run the v3 production step function of proof.md (order-6 GLV automorphism classes, canonical representatives by the single-multiplication method with brute-force cross-checks, partition bump, bounded exceptional retries, distinguished-point trails, split-coordinate scalar bookkeeping under the 36-step rebalancing schedule with split-evaluated reports, collision solving) on a toy curve y^2=x^3+7 over F_786433 with subgroup order 262657, counting TOTAL steps (repeated work included) as the primary metric. The initial (declared) run is the bumped attack configuration: its steps-metric success is 0.627 against the 0.405 target the budget rule (exponent 0.519195) encodes, trapped trails 3, bumps 1753, total additions 59628, 135922 split-state invariant checks and 79800 canonicalisation cross-checks with zero violations. Suggested follow-up inputs within the schema: (a) walk='plain' with otherwise identical inputs (the control: reproduces the v2 experiment's published values exactly -- steps-metric 0.443, 295 trapped trails, 98997 cross-checks -- isolating the bump's effect); (b) mode='census' with walk='plain' and walk='bumped' at J=32 and also at J=16, 64, 128 (trials=1): exact functional-graph censuses whose two-cycle states track N''/(6J) for the plain walk (484/232/106/66 vs 456/228/114/57 predicted) and are 0/0/2/0 for the bumped walk; (c) race configurations mode='attack', J=16, theta_bits=8, detect_cycles=true, trials=200, both walks (trapped trails 2425 plain vs 609 bumped; cap waste 9799654 vs 2431427 steps) and the theta_bits=10 probe (3302 vs 922; 53905812 vs 15001136). This does not establish production curve behavior, production probabilities, memory bounds, or operation costs.

title: secp256k1-ecdlp: Pollard rho over GLV automorphism equivalence classes with a partition-bump step function (v3)
